possibleCauses: Root zone issues such as waterlogging or compaction
Early stages of certain soil-borne pathogens
followUpQuestions: Are the symptoms appearing on the bottom leaves first or the top leaves?
Is the yellowing spreading to the rest of the plant?
How often are you watering the plants and is the soil drainage good?
Have you applied any fertilizers recently?
immediateActions: Check the soil moisture to ensure it is not waterlogged or too dry
Inspect the roots of one affected plant for signs of rot or discoloration
Remove and safely dispose of any severely damaged leaves away from the field
Monitor the plants daily to see if the yellowing spreads to younger leaves
assessment.whenToSeekHelp: Consult a local agricultural extension worker if the yellowing spreads rapidly to the entire plant, if the plant begins to wilt, or if you notice stunted growth, as these could indicate a more serious nutrient imbalance or soil-borne disease.

uncertainty.reason: Interveinal chlorosis can be caused by several different nutrient deficiencies or environmental stressors, and a physical inspection of the soil and root system is necessary to distinguish between them.

checks.name: followUp
checks.detail: expected at least one follow-up question
